title: 324-330 King St N & 329-331 Regina St N (Z-26-19)
body:
ZBA 324-330 King St N & 329-331 Regina St N
Changes to the Zoning Bylaw for this location are required before a permit can be issued. This means that they submit an application that is reviewed by city planners and other agencies before anything can be built.
324 King Waterloo Inc. is proposing to build a new mixed-use building at 324-330 King Street North and 329-331 Regina Street North. The plan includes a 25-storey building containing 226 residential units, 261 bedrooms and a commercial unit along Regina Street North.
Zoning bylaw changes requested include:
reducing the minimum required landscaped open space from 30% to 21%
reducing the minimum tower separation for an interior lot line from 11 m to 9.5 m
reducing the minimum tower stepback above the podium from 3 m to 1.5 m for 40% of the front building façade
to permit structured parking in the podium along the King Street North façade (Section 7.10.10 of the Zoning By-law)
This application is intended to proceed through delegated authority pursuant to City of Waterloo By-law No. 2023-073, which provides the City’s Director of Planning decision making authority for zoning amendments that are deemed to be minor in nature. A public meeting will not be held unless the Director of Planning refers this application to Council.
View the documents submitted by the development company under supporting documents on this page for more details and drawings.
Building height, units, housing types
Building height: 25 storeys
Number of units: 226
Unit sizes: mix of one, two and three bedrooms
Housing types: apartment
Non-residential floor space
Commercial space: 87.19 square m
Parking
Parking: 197 structured parking spaces
Bicycle parking: 156
You can provide feedback to the planning department, and it will be shared with the delegated staff authority, or ask a question to learn more about this application.
Images are provided by the applicant and may not reflect the final design approved by the planning division.
